Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.quote: 9. Warranties.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no limitation of liability, no aggregate cap, and no exclusion of indirect or consequential damages. Searches for "liability", "damages", "consequential", "aggregate", "liable" and "indemnif" return nothing responsive — the only hits are the no-joint-venture language (p0061-p0062) and the Termination Payment calculation (p0026). The Warranties section (p0055-p0058) contains only representations plus a Globix carve-out, and General Provisions (p0059-p0070) has no liability terms. Both parties are therefore exposed to unlimited liability, including the Company for consequential losses arising from Content, marketing and payment matters, so the rule's fallback (mutual 12-month cap with carve-outs) is not met. We inserted the preferred mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees and USD 1,000,000, a mutual consequential-damages waiver, and uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), with the Company's payment obligations (including the Termination Payment) excluded from the cap. Placement as Section 9(c) also picks up the existing survival provision in Section 10.7, which covers Section 9.

Neither Party shall be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages or lost profits. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. The Company's obligations to make payments due under this Agreement (including any Termination Payment) shall not be treated as damages subject to this limitation.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company", customer); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI", host/service provider).

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

input.quote: 9. Warranties.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no limitation of liability, no aggregate cap, and no exclusion of indirect or consequential damages. Searches for "liability", "damages", "consequential", "aggregate", "liable" and "indemnif" return nothing responsive — the only hits are the no-joint-venture language (p0061-p0062) and the Termination Payment calculation (p0026). The Warranties section (p0055-p0058) contains only representations plus a Globix carve-out, and General Provisions (p0059-p0070) has no liability terms. Both parties are therefore exposed to unlimited liability, including the Company for consequential losses arising from Content, marketing and payment matters, so the rule's fallback (mutual 12-month cap with carve-outs) is not met. We inserted the preferred mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees and USD 1,000,000, a mutual consequential-damages waiver, and uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), with the Company's payment obligations (including the Termination Payment) excluded from the cap. Placement as Section 9(c) also picks up the existing survival provision in Section 10.7, which covers Section 9.

input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products
input.rationale: Section 6.1 imposes exclusivity on us (the Company): for the whole term we may not participate in any similar internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, and HDI holds the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer web site. Under Section 4.1 the term is one year but renews automatically each anniversary indefinitely, and exiting requires 90 days' notice plus a Termination Payment under Section 4.2(a), so the restraint effectively runs for the full (open-ended) term with no performance-based release — the only performance exit is the narrow 70-day launch failure right in Section 1.6. That fails the fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic end on HDI's service level/delivery failure) and approaches walk-away territory. Because HDI's development/hosting role and the reciprocal two-year restraint on HDI in Section 6.3 (which benefits us and is left intact) form part of the bargain, we have taken the fallback rather than deleting the covenant: exclusivity is capped at the initial twelve months and ends automatically on HDI's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our playbook does not accept exclusivity binding the Company; at most we can live with a defined product category for twelve months that ends automatically if HDI misses its service levels or delivery dates. We have therefore limited Section 6.1 to the initial one-year term and added an automatic performance-based release, leaving HDI's reciprocal exclusivity in Section 6.3 untouched.
proposal.summary: Limit Company exclusivity to 12 months and add automatic exit on HDI performance failure.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.

Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company", customer); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI", host/service provider).

Rule:
ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Exclusivity limited to a defined product category and 12 months, ending automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

Position — walk-away:
Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.
Detection guidance:
Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback; keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer.

input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products
input.rationale: Section 6.1 imposes exclusivity on us (the Company): for the whole term we may not participate in any similar internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, and HDI holds the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer web site. Under Section 4.1 the term is one year but renews automatically each anniversary indefinitely, and exiting requires 90 days' notice plus a Termination Payment under Section 4.2(a), so the restraint effectively runs for the full (open-ended) term with no performance-based release — the only performance exit is the narrow 70-day launch failure right in Section 1.6. That fails the fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic end on HDI's service level/delivery failure) and approaches walk-away territory. Because HDI's development/hosting role and the reciprocal two-year restraint on HDI in Section 6.3 (which benefits us and is left intact) form part of the bargain, we have taken the fallback rather than deleting the covenant: exclusivity is capped at the initial twelve months and ends automatically on HDI's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

input.quote: 9. Warranties.
input.rationale: Searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless" and "infringe" return nothing, and a full read of Warranties (Section 9) and General Provisions (Section 10) confirms the Agreement contains no indemnity, defence or hold-harmless obligation in either direction. HDI gives no IP infringement indemnity for the Site/Services it builds and hosts, which fails even the fallback and is walk-away territory (Section 7.2's advertising covenant and the confidentiality provisions carry no indemnity). We inserted the vendor-side indemnity as new Section 9(c) covering third-party IP claims, HDI's breach of law, HDI-caused unauthorised disclosure of Company data/Content, and HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics and a carve-out for Company-supplied Content and Marks; no Company indemnity was added.

proposal.summary: Insert HDI indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, data/Content security incidents, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) as new Section 9(c)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no indemnity in either direction, so we have added an HDI indemnity covering third-party IP claims relating to the Site and Services plus HDI's breach of law, unauthorised disclosure of Company data and Content, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics. Our playbook requires the service provider to stand behind third-party claims arising from the services it builds and hosts; we can discuss usual exclusions for Company-supplied Content and Marks if helpful.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company", customer); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI", host/service provider).

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

input.quote: 9. Warranties.
input.rationale:
Searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless", "defend" and "infringe" return nothing, and a full read of the Warranties (Section 9) and General Provisions (Section 10) sections confirms the Agreement contains no indemnity, defence or hold-harmless obligation in either direction — HDI gives no IP infringement indemnity for the Site/Services it builds and hosts, which is walk-away territory under the rule (the mutual advertising covenant in Section 7.2 and the confidentiality obligations do not carry any indemnity). We therefore inserted the vendor-side indemnity as new Section 9(c) covering third-party IP claims, HDI's breach of law, HDI-caused unauthorised disclosure of Company data/Content, and HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics and a carve-out for Company-supplied Content and Marks; we did not add any Company indemnity.</parationale>

input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
input.rationale: Section 6.1 is the only covenant in the Agreement that restrains our side (Section 6.3 restrains HDI, and for two years post-term, which favours us). It sits at the playbook fallback rather than the preferred "no restriction" position, and so is not redlined: (i) it runs "during the term of this Agreement" only, with no post-term tail, and the term under Section 4.1 is one year (auto-renewing, terminable on 90 days' notice), so the restraint never exceeds 12 months without our consent to renew; (ii) scope is limited by product and channel — Internet projects similar to the Site offering Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, with the competing products named (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled) — rather than the walk-away formulation of "any competing business"; and (iii) there is a carve-out in Section 6.2 for a closeout-merchandise site, and "Deerskin Products" itself excludes closeout goods and the Joan Cook Catalog. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted only: there is no express carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (so acquiring a leather retailer that runs a competing site could implicate 6.1), and the words "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" are looser than a purely named-product limit. We would take these as clarifications if the document is reopened for other reasons, but they are not material enough to breach the fallback, and deletion of 6.1 would be disproportionate given HDI's heavier reciprocal restraint in Section 6.3.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company", customer); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI", host/service provider).

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
input.rationale: Section 6.1 is the only covenant in the Agreement that restrains our side (Section 6.3 restrains HDI, and for two years post-term, which favours us). It sits at the playbook fallback rather than the preferred "no restriction" position, and so is not redlined: (i) it runs "during the term of this Agreement" only, with no post-term tail, and the term under Section 4.1 is one year (auto-renewing, terminable on 90 days' notice), so the restraint never exceeds 12 months without our consent to renew; (ii) scope is limited by product and channel — Internet projects similar to the Site offering Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, with the competing products named (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled) — rather than the walk-away formulation of "any competing business"; and (iii) there is a carve-out in Section 6.2 for a closeout-merchandise site, and "Deerskin Products" itself excludes closeout goods and the Joan Cook Catalog. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted only: there is no express carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (so acquiring a leather retailer that runs a competing site could implicate 6.1), and the words "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" are looser than a purely named-product limit. We would take these as clarifications if the document is reopened for other reasons, but they are not material enough to breach the fallback, and deletion of 6.1 would be disproportionate given HDI's heavier reciprocal restraint in Section 6.3.

**Finding submitted: missing (LOL-CAP, critical).**

The agreement is entirely silent on liability. Confirmed across the full document:
- No hits for "damages", "consequential", "liable", "indemnif", "in no event", or any cap language.
- The only "liability" references are the no-joint-venture disclaimers (§10.2), and the only "aggregate" reference is the Termination Payment formula (§4.2).
- Warranties (§9) covers authority reps and the Globix carve-out only; General Provisions (§10) has no liability terms.

Both parties are exposed to unlimited liability, so even the fallback (mutual 12-month cap with indemnity/confidentiality/gross-negligence carve-outs) is unmet.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** new §9(c) inserting the preferred mutual cap — greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable by the Company and USD 1,000,000 — plus a mutual consequential-damages waiver, uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and confirmation that the Company's payment obligations (including the Termination Payment) are not capped damages. Placing it in §9 means it survives under the existing §10.7 survival list, and the comment offers a straight 12-months'-fees cap as the fallback.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant (at fallback) — no redline proposed.**

Section 6.1 is the only restrictive covenant binding the Company; I swept the body for other restraints ("shall not", "may not", "exclusive", "compete") and found none directed at our side. Section 6.3 restrains HDI (two years post-term), which benefits us and is not flagged.

Why 6.1 clears the fallback:
- **Term-only:** expressly "during the term of this Agreement," with no post-term tail; Section 4.1 sets a one-year term (auto-renewing, 90 days' notice), so the restraint never exceeds 12 months absent our own renewal.
- **Defined, narrow scope:** limited to Internet projects similar to the Site offering Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, with the competing products named (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled) — not the walk-away "any competing business." Our catalog and retail channels are untouched.
- **Carve-out present:** Section 6.2 preserves a closeout-merchandise site, and "Deerskin Products" itself excludes closeout goods and the Joan Cook Catalog.

Noted but not redlined (minor sub-elements per playbook semantics): no express internal-development/acquisition carve-out, so acquiring a leather retailer that operates a competing site could implicate 6.1; and "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" is looser than a strictly named-product limit. Worth picking up as clarifications if the document reopens for other reasons — deleting 6.1 outright would be disproportionate given HDI's heavier reciprocal restraint in 6.3.

**Finding: missing (critical) — no indemnification anywhere in the Agreement.**

- Searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless", "defend" and "infringe" returned nothing; a full read of Section 9 (Warranties) and Section 10 (General Provisions) confirms there is no defence, indemnity or hold-harmless obligation running in either direction. Section 7.2's mutual advertising covenant and the Section 8 confidentiality obligations carry no indemnity, and there is no limitation-of-liability section either.
- HDI builds, hosts and distributes the Site and supplies the platform, software and administration tools, so the absence of any HDI IP-infringement indemnity leaves us fully exposed to third-party claims on infrastructure we do not control — this fails even the fallback position and sits in walk-away territory.
- Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted: new **Section 9(c)** inserted after p0058, requiring HDI to defend and indemnify the Company and its affiliates for (1) IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Site, Services or HDI-provided materials (carved out where the claim arises from Company-supplied Content or Marks), (2) HDI's breach of law, (3) HDI-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of Content, user information or Company data, and (4) HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice, defence-control (consent required for settlements binding us) and cooperation mechanics.
- Deliberately no reciprocal Company indemnity was added; the Company-side carve-out for our own Content and Marks is the concession offered if HDI pushes back.

You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

input.rationale: Section 6.1 imposes exclusivity on us (the Company): for the whole term we may not participate in any similar internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, and HDI holds the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer web site. Under Section 4.1 the term is one year but renews automatically each anniversary indefinitely, and exiting requires 90 days' notice plus a Termination Payment under Section 4.2(a), so the restraint effectively runs for the full (open-ended) term with no performance-based release — the only performance exit is the narrow 70-day launch failure right in Section 1.6. That fails the fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic end on HDI's service level/delivery failure) and approaches walk-away territory. Because HDI's development/hosting role and the reciprocal two-year restraint on HDI in Section 6.3 (which benefits us and is left intact) form part of the bargain, we have taken the fallback rather than deleting the covenant: exclusivity is capped at the initial twelve months and ends automatically on HDI's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products
input.rationale: Section 6.1 imposes exclusivity on us (the Company): for the whole term we may not participate in any similar internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, and HDI holds the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer web site. Under Section 4.1 the term is one year but renews automatically each anniversary indefinitely, and exiting requires 90 days' notice plus a Termination Payment under Section 4.2(a), so the restraint effectively runs for the full (open-ended) term with no performance-based release — the only performance exit is the narrow 70-day launch failure right in Section 1.6. That fails the fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic end on HDI's service level/delivery failure) and approaches walk-away territory. Because HDI's development/hosting role and the reciprocal two-year restraint on HDI in Section 6.3 (which benefits us and is left intact) form part of the bargain, we have taken the fallback rather than deleting the covenant: exclusivity is capped at the initial twelve months and ends automatically on HDI's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company", customer); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI", host/service provider).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Deviation — EXCLUSIVITY (Section 6.1)**

- **Issue:** Section 6.1 binds us, the Company, not to participate in any similar internet project for Deerskin Products (or substantially similar products) "during the term of this Agreement," while granting HDI the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer site.
- **Why it fails the fallback:** Section 4.1 makes the term evergreen (one year, auto-renewing on each anniversary), and exit requires 90 days' notice plus a Termination Payment under Section 4.2(a). So the restraint runs for the full open-ended term with no automatic performance-based release; the only performance exit is the narrow 70-day launch-failure right in Section 1.6.
- **Left intact:** Section 6.3 (two-year restraint on HDI) and Section 6.2 (closeout-site carve-out) benefit us and were not touched.
- **Redline (validated, fallback level):** exclusivity capped at the initial twelve months from the Effective Date, excluding renewal terms, plus automatic termination of our obligation, without payment or penalty, on HDI's failure to meet any service level, launch date or delivery date.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule: EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer

Preferred position:
No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.

Fallback position:
Exclusivity limited to a defined product category and 12 months, ending automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.


Drafter's locked target level: fallback

Original clause:
4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").
6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.

Rendered redlined clause:
4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").
6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the twelve (12) month period commencing on the Effective Date (and not during any renewal term), the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet. The Company's obligations under this Section 6.1 shall terminate automatically, without payment or penalty, upon HDI's failure to meet any service level, launch date or other delivery date set forth in this Agreement.

input.quote: This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other.
input.rationale: Section 4.1 provides one-year automatic renewals (acceptable term length) but requires ninety (90) days' written notice to stop a renewal. That exceeds the fallback ceiling of a 60-day non-renewal notice window, so it fails the fallback on a material term, though it stops short of walk-away territory (windows longer than 90 days or multi-year auto-renewals). We therefore propose the minimal edit to the preferred 30-day window; the fallback of 60 days is offered in the comment. No renewal price-uplift language appears anywhere in the Agreement, and the absence of a vendor renewal reminder is a minor sub-element noted here rather than separately flagged.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company", customer); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI", host/service provider).

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

input.quote: This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other.
input.rationale: Section 4.1 provides one-year automatic renewals (acceptable term length) but requires ninety (90) days' written notice to stop a renewal. That exceeds the fallback ceiling of a 60-day non-renewal notice window, so it fails the fallback on a material term, though it stops short of walk-away territory (windows longer than 90 days or multi-year auto-renewals). We therefore propose the minimal edit to the preferred 30-day window; the fallback of 60 days is offered in the comment. No renewal price-uplift language appears anywhere in the Agreement, and the absence of a vendor renewal reminder is a minor sub-element noted here rather than separately flagged.

input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Section 4.1 gives either Party a convenience exit on 90 days' written notice against a one-year auto-renewing term, which sits at our fallback on notice period and on HDI's symmetrical (end-of-term) right — that element we do not redline. The material failure is Section 4.2: if the Company terminates, it owes an uncapped Termination Payment equal to 50% of Net Sales above $800,000 for the trailing twelve months, payable over eight quarterly installments. Because fees to HDI are only 30% of Net Sales above $11,000 per month, that formula can exceed a full year's fees and far exceeds the fallback ceiling of three months' fees, so the Company has no genuinely penalty-free exit. We therefore capped the Termination Payment at three months' fees (fallback rather than preferred, given HDI's site build investment and the revenue-share bargain).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We capped the Termination Payment at three months' fees, since as drafted it is an uncapped share of Net Sales that operates as a penalty on a routine non-renewal. Our playbook position is termination for convenience without penalty; the three-month cap is our fallback and reflects HDI's build investment.
proposal.summary: Cap the Company's Termination Payment at three months' fees.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company", customer); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI", host/service provider).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.

Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, T4C).**

**What the document does:**
- **§ 4.1 (p0024)** — one-year term, auto-renewing annually, terminable by *either* Party on 90 days' written notice effective at an anniversary. On notice period and on HDI's end-of-term-only convenience right, this **sits at our fallback** and I did not redline it.
- **§ 4.2 (p0026, p0029)** — but if *the Company* terminates, it owes a "Termination Payment" of 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, payable in eight quarterly installments.

**Why it fails the fallback:** fees to HDI are only 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month (§ 3.1), so the termination formula can readily exceed a full year of fees — well beyond the fallback ceiling of three months' fees. The result is that the Company's nominal convenience right is not penalty-free, which is the substance the rule protects.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** a proviso capping the Termination Payment at three months' fees under § 3.1. I used the **fallback rather than preferred** (no penalty at all) because HDI carries the site build and programming costs and the deal is a revenue share — deleting the payment outright would be disproportionate to the existing bargain.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

messages.content:
Rule: T4C — Termination for convenience

Preferred position:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.


Fallback position:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.


Drafter's locked target level: fallback

Original clause:
4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").
(a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
(c) The Termination Payment, if any, shall be payable by the Company in eight (8) equal payments to be made quarterly, commencing thirty (30) days after the termination date.

Rendered redlined clause:
4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from the supplied source. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change.

This is a bounded short-document repair and you have no tools. The user supplies the exact source paragraphs, definitions, current proposal, and deterministic feedback. Return only the requested structured proposal and one-to-one element coverage. Copy every replace.oldText byte-for-byte from a supplied paragraph. Do not invent an anchor or source text.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule prose and exact atomic checklist:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company", customer); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI", host/service provider).

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.
